content:
Country music will stop what it's doing tonight. Nearly two months after Dolly Parton's death at age 80, the Country Music Association's star-studded live tribute — "CMA Presents I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton" — airs from Belmont University's Fisher Center for the Performing Arts in Nashville at 8 p.m. Central on ABC and Disney+.

That's the headline. Here's everything verified so far.

The lineup

Twenty performers are confirmed: Ashley McBryde, Béla Fleck, Brad Paisley, Carly Pearce, Carrie Underwood, Darius Rucker, Ella Langley, Kelsea Ballerini, Kristen Bell, Kristin Chenoweth, Lady A, Lainey Wilson, Little Big Town, Lukas Nelson, Molly Tuttle, Reba McEntire, Ricky Skaggs, Sierra Hull, Vince Gill and Zac Brown. Special guests Amy Grant and Kimberly Williams-Paisley will appear, and a Belmont University student ensemble will join a performance. According to the CMA, tickets are sold out, though limited premium experiences remain.

The show will also feature archival footage and stories tracing Parton's journey from East Tennessee to the world's biggest stages.

How to watch

The two-hour special airs live Wednesday, Oct. 21 at 9 p.m. Eastern — 8 p.m. Central — on ABC and Disney+, and will be available to stream the following day on Disney+ and Hulu.

Why this one matters

Parton died on Aug. 25 after a brief battle with cancer, and tributes have been rolling in ever since. But this is the first major televised celebration of her life, produced by the CMA itself. It lands barely eight weeks after her death — fast by industry standards, which tells you how eager the business was to honor her. Watch the audience, not just the stage: when artists of this caliber clear their schedules for a Wednesday night in October, the industry is telling you something about who mattered.
